Varenicline, a drug used for smoking cessation, is known to interact with the neuronal acetylcholine receptor subunit beta-3, which in turn is a target of ethanol. This creates a chain of interactions where varenicline may influence the activity of the acetylcholine receptor subunit alpha-9 through its effects on the beta-3 subunit. The final score of 0.6782 indicates a moderate level of confidence in this relationship, supported by the sequential targeting of the subunits. However, the evidence is indirect and relies on the assumption that the interaction between varenicline and beta-3 subunit is sufficient to modulate alpha-9 subunit function. Further experimental validation would be necessary to confirm this mechanism.
